To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the three approaches to jet quenching that we have studied all give a reasonable description of the data, but that the values of $\stackrel{\hat{}}{q}/T^{3}$ required to describe the data vary by a factor of 2 between approaches.
all three approaches can be tuned to provide a good fit of the available data.

the BDMPS-Z/ ASW, the HT and the AMY approaches are all able to provide a good fit to inclusive data on ${\mathit{R}}_{{\mathit{A}}\mathit{a}}$, but that their predictions differ for the centrality, and azimuthal angular, dependence of ${R}_{{\mathit{\mathit{A}}}a}$ vs ${\mathit{\mathrm{p}}}_{{\mathbf{T}}}$
In summary, our research is concerned with
the systematic investigation of the effects of different jet energy-loss schemes on the observables of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP).

the following: (1) the comparison of different jet energy-loss schemes using the same realistic RFD simulation, (2) the determination of the values of the relevant transport parameters in the different schemes, (3) the comparison of the different schemes in their ability to describe the data on the centrality and angular dependence of ${\mathrm{d}}{E}∕{\mathrm{d}}{\mathit{y}}$ and ${R}_{\mathrm{AA}}$, (4)
the comparison of the predictions of three approaches to jet quenching.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all three approaches are in good agreement with the data, and the differences between the approaches are not large enough to rule out any of them.
all three approaches provide a good qualitative description of the data and are consistent with each other, but that there is a need for a more detailed quantitative comparison.

, while all three approaches are able to provide a good fit to the data on ${R}_{{\mathit{dE/dx}}}$, ${R}_{\mathrm{AA}}$ and $v_{2}$, the values of the free parameters of these approaches are not universal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BDMPS-Z/AMW scheme is more consistent with the data than the higher twist (BDMPS/Z) approach and the AMW approach.
all three approaches can be tuned to give a reasonable description of inclusive data for ${R}_{\mathrm{AA}}$ but that they do not agree with each other in detail.
the HT and AMY approaches are more consistent with the data than the ASW approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three approaches to jet energy loss are not only qualitatively but also quantitatively different from each other.

all the approaches considered here can be used to provide a good fit to the inclusive data, and thus the differences between them are likely not significant enough to allow for a definitive choice of one approach over another.

, while there is still room for further improvement, the three approaches considered in our paper are already able to provide a reasonably good description of inclusive jet suppression data in a wide range of transverse momentum, centrality and azimuth.
